# libdiginet / fuzz_decode

libdiginet's own fuzz target `fuzz_decode` ([source](source/fuzz_decode.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libdiginet 0.1.1 (FreeMixer/libdiginet at 835f336c).

The first byte picks a desk type (none, Control|24 or ProControl) and whether the rest is a whole Ethernet frame or just a frame body; the rest is copied into an allocation of its exact length, and in frame mode the body the grammar reads in it is used. The harness steps through the command stream with the library cursor and decoder and with its own reader written from the protocol grammar, comparing every message, refusal, cursor position and decoded control, and checks the system-family refusal of the whole body. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libdiginet at commit 835f336c: the frame, command cursor, controls and decoder sources and the session state machine, built into one static library. The packet socket and descriptor io are not built; the library's own libFuzzer build uses the same sources.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The command cursor gives each step the grammar gives: the end only at the end, each message with its place, length, status, running-status flag and data bytes or sysex payload, and each refusal with the cursor and running status the grammar leaves ([lines 41-115](source/fuzz_decode.c#L41-L115)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The decoder turns each step into the control the protocol documentation describes (keys, touches, faders with their low byte, jog and V-Pot deltas, rings, meters, LEDs, scribble and counter writes, system and other messages), with every field right ([lines 152-263](source/fuzz_decode.c#L152-L263)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The body check refuses a body exactly when it holds the system-family sequence F0 13 xx 70, whole or cut short ([lines 265-276](source/fuzz_decode.c#L265-L276)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libdiginet` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_decode.plain` | 48,808 | `d570b4c96d9e764af0482c34642d2e58e6eef3af84e768d2a076a56eaeb045a7` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_decode.ubsan` | 49,312 | `cfe3a2ee2a54a9693cae0c77632e069b3e7dd8ae01a8a8c25258faa955a31f71` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
